clue.text: Took notice of man with awful deed

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: awful suggests the word deed is mangled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone paid attention to a man who had done something terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention, so having heeded is having taken notice.

clue.text: I reportedly will embrace vile malevolent gaze

indicators.note: will embrace means the spoken form of I wraps around the next word, vile
reportedly signals we go by how the word I is spoken, not written

parts.note: the letter I is said aloud the same as the organ of sight

explanation.surface: A claim that someone will take hold of a vile, spiteful stare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is not taken as a letter but as a spoken word whose sound matches the organ of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a look believed to bring harm or bad luck to its target.

clue.text: Twelve work at Buddhist faith

parts.note: to do a task is to work at it
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: Someone works at mastering Buddhism twelve times over.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is a group or count of twelve.

clue.text: Lower the dignity of church official embracing me

indicators.note: embracing says the word for the cleric goes around the word me

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric in a cathedral

explanation.surface: A complaint that a cleric's hug has robbed the speaker of dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade or belittle them.

clue.text: Nothing New York Times gave for stone

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: The New York Times handed over a gemstone for free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York Times' reads as the newspaper, but splits into NY and X, the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Treading the boards, male only falls into one

indicators.note: falls into says the men-only word drops inside the word one

parts.note: a stag party or stag night is for men only

explanation.surface: An actor on stage, the only man present, takes a tumble into somebody.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread the boards is to perform as an actor, that is to be in front of an audience in a theatre.

clue.text: Long time before end of reign

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word reign

explanation.surface: A monarch's reign lasting a long time before it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about the reign, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, a synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Loathe a taste of crab hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: a taste of says only a small sample of the following words is wanted, here a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A diner who hates even a bite of the crab starter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest or hate it strongly.

clue.text: Auctions off prison rooms, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for prison rooms is taken as spoken

parts.note: prisoners are kept in cells

explanation.surface: A report that a jail is putting its rooms up for auction.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a way of selling goods to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Left in pieces when hearing prolonged bombing

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the other piece
when hearing says the word for pieces is taken as spoken, its final S sounding like Z

parts.note: bits are pieces

explanation.surface: A building left in fragments after a sustained aerial attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when hearing' turns BITS into BITZ; 'in' puts L inside: B-L-ITZ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blitz was the long German bombing campaign on Britain in 1940-41; the word now means any intense sustained attack.

clue.text: Motorway share is an error

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
one's take is one's share of the proceeds

explanation.surface: Splitting the cost of a motorway is a bad idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is a wrong action or judgement, a synonym of error.

clue.text: South Pacific islands seen from a canoe I upset

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of a canoe I are tipped over and rearranged, as a capsized boat

explanation.surface: A paddler capsizes and views the Pacific islands from the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region name covering the islands of the central and South Pacific.

clue.text: Cancel book, not author's first

indicators.note: not says the following letter is removed from the book word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word author's

explanation.surface: An instruction to call off a book, though not the writer's debut.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, the first letter of 'author's', from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, to cancel it.

clue.text: Mushy peas containing one brown pigment

indicators.note: containing says the scrambled letters hold the numeral for one
mushy implies the word peas is mashed up into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Mushy peas that have a brownish colouring agent in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushy' makes SEPA from PEAS; 'containing' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the reddish-brown pigment originally taken from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Eroding ruin paid no heed

indicators.note: ruin suggests the word Eroding is wrecked and rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone overlooked the erosion that was destroying a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ignored something is to have taken no notice of it.

clue.text: Lacerates eye secretions

definitions.meaning: to lacerate is to rip or rend, a verb said 'tares'
the salty drops that come from crying

explanation.surface: Wounds that make the eyes water.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling, two words: the verb to rip and the plural noun for drops from the eyes.

clue.text: Reunite characters in train

indicators.note: characters in says the letters of Reunite are taken out and arranged anew

explanation.surface: Bringing the cast of a show back together on a railway journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway, but means a body of followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is the group of attendants following an important person, which is what a retinue is.

clue.text: Pay out to put page in post

indicators.note: put marks the letter for page being placed somewhere
in says that place is inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Paying to have a page sent by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money is to pay it out.

clue.text: Council raged and held up bulb

indicators.note: up says the held letters are read upwards, backwards in a down entry
held says the letters are contained within the words Council raged

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A council was furious and delayed a matter concerning a bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'held up' as one reversal signal, leaving the hidden word with no indicator; 'held' is the hiding signal and 'up' the reversal, giving CILRAG read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic grows as a bulb made of cloves, used in cooking.

clue.text: Funny old penny loaf

parts.note: D stood for the penny in pre-decimal British money (from Latin denarius)
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: An amusing old price of a penny for a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means dryly amusing or whimsical.

clue.text: Park throws out only tall supporter

parts.note: P is the map abbreviation for a car park

indicators.note: throws out suggests the word only is flung about into a new order

explanation.surface: A park ejects the only big fan it had.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel tower that holds up power cables.

clue.text: Arm over for bar dance?

parts.note: an arm is a limb
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A question whether an arm slung over a bar is part of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbo is the dance in which performers lean back to pass under a lowered bar.

clue.text: Accomplice has a chance to repent, initially

parts.note: a bet is a chance or gamble, as in a good bet

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word repent

explanation.surface: A criminal's partner gets an opportunity to say sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor helps or encourages someone to commit a crime, an accomplice.

clue.text: Small fish constantly circling lake

indicators.note: circling says the word for constantly goes around the letter for lake

parts.note: ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: A little fish swimming round and round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a small fish.

clue.text: Figure manure was spread on lake

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters of manure are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A man spreading fertiliser beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a symbol for a number, a figure.

clue.text: Mercenary victory on back road

parts.note: V is for victory

indicators.note: back says the word for road is read backwards

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A soldier for hire wins and then heads back down the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercenary' looks like a noun, but is the adjective: open to bribery.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal means motivated by money and open to bribery, as mercenary is used of people.

clue.text: Deity admits nothing fine

indicators.note: admits says the word for deity lets the zero letter inside

parts.note: a deity is a god
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A god confesses that nothing is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and good are synonyms of approval: satisfactory, of decent quality.

clue.text: Escort turns to supporter

indicators.note: turns to suggests the word Escort is twisted round into another form

explanation.surface: A companion turns to a friend for backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' suggests a backer, but means a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a tight undergarment that supports the torso.
